bottom_line: In APPRAISE-2, apixaban 5 mg twice daily plus antiplatelet therapy versus placebo plus antiplatelet therapy did not reduce the primary efficacy outcome (hazard ratio, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.80 to 1.11) but increased TIMI major bleeding (hazard ratio, 2.59; 95% CI, 1.50 to 4.46).
implications: These data support that, in this trial population, adding apixaban to antiplatelet therapy did not show a statistically significant reduction in cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or ischemic stroke (hazard ratio, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.80 to 1.11; P = 0.51) and was associated with higher TIMI major bleeding (hazard ratio, 2.59; 95% CI, 1.50 to 4.46; P = 0.001), including more intracranial bleeding (12 vs. 3) and fatal bleeding (5 vs. 0).

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial comparing apixaban vs placebo added to standard antiplatelet therapy after recent ACS in high-risk patients.
major_points.quote: We conducted a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial comparing apixaban, at a dose of 5 mg twice daily, with placebo, in addition to standard antiplatelet therapy, in patients with a recent acute coronary syndrome

major_points.text: The trial was terminated early due to excess major bleeding with apixaban without a counterbalancing reduction in recurrent ischemic events.
major_points.quote: The trial was terminated prematurely after recruitment of 7392 patients because of an increase in major bleeding events with apixaban in the absence of a counterbalanc- ing reduction in recurrent ischemic events.

major_points.text: Primary efficacy outcome was cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or ischemic stroke.
major_points.quote: The primary efficacy outcome was the composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or ischemic stroke.

major_points.text: Intracranial bleeding occurred more often with apixaban than placebo.

Intracranial bleeding occurred in 12 (0.3) with apixaban and 3 (0.1) with placebo.

harms.text: TIMI major bleeding occurred more often with apixaban than placebo (46 [1.3%] vs 18 [0.5%]; hazard ratio 2.59).
Fatal bleeding events occurred with apixaban but not placebo (5 vs 0).
Intracranial bleeding was more frequent with apixaban (12 [0.3] vs 3 [0.1]; hazard ratio 4.06).
More patients stopped study drug before end of trial in apixaban group than placebo (23.5% vs 20.5%).
harms.quote: 863 of the 3673 patients who received at least one dose of apixaban (23.5%) and 746 of the 3642 who received at least one dose of placebo (20.5%) stopped taking the study drug before the end of the trial

harms.text: Serious adverse events and overall adverse events were similar between groups.
harms.quote: The frequencies of serious adverse events and overall adverse events were similar in the apixaban group and the placebo group (24.3% and 59.0%, respectively, in the apixaban group and 24.3% and 57.7%, respectively, in the placebo group).
